air quality policy can be a powerful tool in fire management, but only if it is developed and implemented with a clear understanding of the science and policy of fire and smoke, and the social-ecological context in which they operate.
air quality regulations can constrain wildland fire management goals, and that fire managers must be aware of these constraints to effectively manage wildland fires.

air quality and fire management policy development should occur in parallel to maximise the potential for effective, integrated policies.
